name: ClickFix (Fake CAPTCHA / Verification Social Engineering)
description: ClickFix is a social-engineering technique in which a compromised or malicious webpage displays a fake CAPTCHA or 'verify you are human' prompt that instructs the victim to press Win+R, paste a clipboard-injected command, and hit Enter — bypassing the browser sandbox entirely by tricking the user into manually executing PowerShell or mshta commands. Originally a criminal infostealer delivery method (StealC, Lumma, Amatera), it has since been adopted by state-sponsored actors including Kimsuky, APT28, and MuddyWater for espionage operations, and Halcyon's ROC logged over 10 pre-ransomware ClickFix incidents in March-April 2026 alone. A May 2026 Malwarebytes report documented 700+ compromised education and tech websites delivering ClickFix lures via a SQL-injection campaign (CVE-2026-26980), while the IClickFix WordPress framework has hit 3,800+ sites across 82 countries since late 2024. Recent variants leverage signed Microsoft App-V scripts and the Donut shellcode framework to evade EDR while delivering infostealers and RATs like modeloRAT.

mitre_techniques.technique_name: User Execution: Malicious Copy and Paste
mitre_techniques.notes: Core mechanism — JavaScript silently writes a malicious command to the clipboard for the victim to paste and run
Pasted command typically launches an obfuscated PowerShell one-liner via the Run dialog
Some ClickFix variants use mshta.exe to execute remotely-hosted malicious HTA/JS payloads
Variants abuse signed Microsoft App-V (AppV) sequencer scripts as living-off-the-land binaries to proxy script execution

mitre_techniques.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Embedded Payloads
mitre_techniques.notes: Payloads are GZip-compressed/encrypted and decompressed in-memory before execution via Invoke-Expression
Victims are directed to the fake CAPTCHA page via phishing emails or malicious/compromised websites

notable_examples: May 2026 Malwarebytes report: 700+ education/tech websites compromised via CVE-2026-26980 SQL injection to serve ClickFix fake CAPTCHA pages
January 2026 TheHackerNews report on ClickFix campaigns abusing signed Microsoft App-V scripts and trusted CDNs to deliver Amatera Stealer via Donut-generated shellcode
Kimsuky (Jan-Feb 2025, ongoing into 2026) targeted North Korea policy think tanks with fake secure-drive 'registration' prompts leading to QuasarRAT via ClickFix
APT28/UNK_RemoteRogue used a fake Google Spreadsheet + reCAPTCHA ClickFix lure to set up SSH tunnels and deploy Metasploit
Halcyon Ransomware Operations Center logged 10+ pre-ransomware ClickFix intrusions across client environments in March-April 2026, signaling adoption by ransomware affiliates ahead of encryption
detection_opportunities: Monitor for Win+R (RunMRU registry key) entries followed immediately by execution of powershell.exe, mshta.exe, or msiexec.exe with long encoded/obfuscated arguments
Alert on clipboard-to-Run-dialog execution chains — explorer.exe spawning a script interpreter with base64 or compressed payload arguments
Detect signed Microsoft App-V (AppV) sequencer binaries being invoked with non-standard scripts as a script-execution proxy
Block or restrict mshta.exe execution where not required by business applications
User awareness training: legitimate CAPTCHAs (Google, Cloudflare, hCaptcha) never instruct users to open the Run dialog, Terminal, or PowerShell
Hunt for outbound connections to legitimate CDNs/blockchain-based services immediately following PowerShell execution (used for evasive C2/staging)
Apply web filtering/EDR rules for known ClickFix page indicators (fake 'I'm not a robot' verification overlays requesting keyboard shortcuts)
